source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Mechanical V8, p.6-29

procedures.title: Hydraulic valve lifters: locate noisy lifter
steps: When one or more lifters are noisy, remove all lifters, take them apart, clean them in solvent, reassemble and reinstall them.
notes: Intermittent clicking: a tiny bit of dirt briefly caught between ball seat and check ball, rarely an out-of-round or flat-spotted ball, or wrong adjustment.
Dirt, corrosion or carbon found in one lifter is very likely in all of them.

procedures.title: Valve lifters (V8): remove and install
steps: Pull the lifters, keeping them in a rack so each returns to its own bore.
Installation: fit the lifters, coating the foot of any new lifter with Molykote or equivalent.
Install and adjust the valve mechanism.

procedures.title: Valve stem oil seal and/or valve spring (V8): replace
steps: Remove the spark plug, rocker arm and push rod for each cylinder being worked on.
Put compressed air into the plug hole to hold the valves up.
Compress the spring with Tool J-5892 and remove the locks, cap, spring and damper (see figure 6V in the manual).
Remove the valve stem oil seal.

327 (and 302, 307, 350): place the spring and damper (close-coiled end against the head), shield and cap, compress with J-5892, fit the seal flat and untwisted in the lower stem groove (a little oil helps), then fit the locks and release, checking the locks seat in the upper groove.
427 (and 396): fit a new oiled stem seal over the guide, place the spring and damper and cap, compress with J-5892, fit the locks and release, checking the locks seat in the groove.
notes: An air adapter can be bought from local jobbers or made: knock the porcelain out of an AC-46N plug (chisel it and tap the center electrode on a hard block), then cut 3/8" pipe threads in the shell (see figure 5V in the manual); this fits all Chevrolet engines.
Grease can hold the locks while the compressor is released.
